newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN RUPEE ENDS UP, FORWARD DLR PREMIUMS FALL.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN RUPEE ENDS UP, FORWARD DLR PREMIUMS FALL.

text.p: The forward dollar premiums fell on Thursday but the spot rupee ended up at 35.7050/7150 despite Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervention, dealers said.
The spot dollar opened the day steady at 35.715/725 rupees.
Dealers said premiums fell sharply on forward dollar sales at higher levels.
"Besides, quite a few traders had booked forwards anticipating the RBI will buy forward dollars and push premiums up," said a public sector bank dealer.
This did not happen. One banker said he heard RBI bought January dollars towards the close of the market but other banks could not confirm RBI's forward dollar purchases on Thursday.
"The forward market saw profit-booking and loss cutting today," said the chief dealer at a public sector bank.
"In a perfect market, spot rate and premiums will move in tandem and adjust according to interest rate differentials," said a dealer.
The Indian market being imperfect, only forward premiums rose on large RBI intervention this week even as the spot rupee gained against the dollar, he said.
"The RBI succeeded in creating some volatility and panic among those with dollar liabilities -- importers and those with foreign exchange loan exposure," he said.
In the spot section, there was little demand for dollars except from the central bank.
The RBI began buying at 35.7175 and later brought down the price to 35.7150 and finally to 35.7125, dealers said.
The six month annualised forward premium closed Thursday at 4.59 percent compared to the previous close of 5.04 percent.
